He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]]. ==Early life and career== Ayayi was born and raised in [[Bordeaux]], France. Growing up, he idolized [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) player and Bordeaux native [[Boris Diaw]].{{cite web |last1=Lawson |first1=Theo |title=Gonzaga's Killian Tillie and Joel Ayayi meet French icon, idol Boris Diaw after Baylor win |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2019/mar/23/gonzagas-killian-tillie-and-joel-ayayi-meet-french/ |website=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |accessdate=24 September 2019 |date=23 March 2019}} Ayayi attended [[INSEP]], a sports institute in [[Paris]], and played for affiliated club [[Centre Fédéral de Basket-ball|Centre Fédéral]].{{cite web |last1=Hein |first1=David |title=CFBB's Ayayi learns from big sister |url=https://www.adidasngt.com/u18/news/latest/i/7rrmjb6qiyqvramw/cfbb-s-ayayi-learns-from-big-sister |publisher=[[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament|Adidas Next Generation tournament]] |accessdate=24 September 2019 |date=27 April 2017}} ===Recruiting=== He was considered a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] and received [[NCAA Division I]] offers from [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]], [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]], and [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]].{{cite web |title=Joel Ayayi, 2017 Point guard |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2017/joel-ayayi-197482 |publisher=[[Rivals.com]] |accessdate=24 September 2019}} On 27 April 2017, Ayayi committed to play [[college basketball]] for Gonzaga.{{cite web |last1=Woodburn |first1=Peter |title=2017 Recruiting: French guard Joel Ayayi commits to Gonzaga [http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/229258/joe-ayayi ESPN] ==College career== Ayayi joined the Gonzaga basketball team at age 17 and [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] his first season to train with the team.{{cite web |last1=Laurin |first1=Emmanuel |title=Joël Ayayi, ou la découverte de la NCAA à 17 ans |url=https://www.basketusa.com/news/459908/joel-ayayi-ou-la-decouverte-de-la-ncaa-a-17-ans/ |publisher=Basket USA |accessdate=24 September 2019 |language=French |date=2 December 2017}} In his redshirt freshman season, he averaged 5.6 minutes per game through 23 contests.{{cite web |title=Joel Ayayi |url=https://gozags.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=2521 |publisher=Gonzaga University Athletics |accessdate=24 September 2019}} On 27 November 2019, early in his sophomore season, Ayayi posted 21 points, 12 rebounds and six assists in a win over [[Southern Miss Golden Eagles basketball|Southern Miss]].{{cite web |last1=Beard |first1=Aaron |title=Kispert, No. 8 Gonzaga top Southern Miss 94-69 at Atlantis |url=https://apnews.com/de4fc396adb849fca09afafd330dc835 |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |accessdate=18 December 2019 |date=28 November 2019}} He had 20 points in a 94–50 win over [[San Diego Toreros men's basketball|San Diego]] on 9 January 2020.{{cite news |last1=Hines |first1=Travis |title=Filip Petrusev, No. 1 Gonzaga race past San Diego 94–50 |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2020/01/10/filip-petrusev-no-1-gonzaga-race-past-san-diego-94-50/ |accessdate=10 January 2020 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=10 January 2020}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Ayayi was named Honorable Mention All-[[West Coast Conference]] (WCC).{{cite press release|url=https://wccsports.com/news/2020/3/3/wcc-announces-2019-20-mens-basketball-all-conference-team-mbb.aspx |title=WCC Announces 2019-20 Men's Basketball All-Conference Team |publisher=West Coast Conference |date=3 March 2020 |accessdate=3 March 2020}} On 10 March, he helped Gonzaga win the [[2020 West Coast Conference men's basketball tournament|WCC tournament]] and was named Most Outstanding Player after scoring 17 points in the final against [[Saint Mary's Gaels men's basketball|Saint Mary's]].{{cite web |title=Zags Crowned WCC Tournament Champs |url=https://gozags.com/news/2020/3/10/mens-basketball-zags-crowned-wcc-tournament-champs.aspx |website=Gonzaga University Athletics |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |accessdate=11 March 2020 |date=10 March 2020}} He averaged 10.6 points, 6.3 rebounds, and 3.2 per game for the Bulldogs and was All-WCC honorable mention. Following the season he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]] but did not hire an agent.{{cite news |last1=Meehan |first1=Jim |title=Joel Ayayi declares for NBA draft but indicates No. 1 option is returning to Gonzaga |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2020/apr/25/gonzagas-joel-ayayi-declares-for-nba-draft-but-won/ |accessdate=27 April 2020 |work=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |date=25 April 2020}} On 1 August, Ayayi announced he was withdrawing from the draft and returning for his junior season.{{cite news |title=Gonzaga's Joel Ayayi withdraws from NBA draft, will return to school for junior season |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29578675/gonzaga-joel-ayayi-withdraws-nba-draft-return-school-junior-season |accessdate=2 August 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=1 August 2020}} Coming into his junior season, Ayayi was named to the Preseason All-WCC team.{{cite web |title=Gonzaga Picked to Win Ninth Straight WCC Championship |url=https://wccsports.com/news/2020/10/25/mens-basketball-gonzaga-picked-to-win-ninth-straight-wcc-championship.aspx |website=[[West Coast Conference]] |accessdate=7 November 2020 |date=26 October 2020}} On 9 January 2021, he recorded the first [[triple-double]] in program history, with 12 points, 13 rebounds and 14 assists in a 116–88 win over [[Portland Pilots men's basketball|Portland]]. He also tallied the second-most assists for a Gonzaga player in a single game.{{cite web |last1=Greene |first1=Brenna |title=Joel Ayayi becomes first Gonzaga player ever to record a triple-double in Gonzaga win |url=https://www.krem.com/article/sports/gonzaga-bulldogs/joel-ayayi-becomes-first-gonzaga-player-ever-to-record-a-triple-double-in-gonzaga-win/293-c1690683-5801-4354-ad1c-318e0f467472 |website=[[KREM (TV)]] |access-date=10 January 2021 |date=9 January 2021}} As a junior, he averaged 12 points, 6.9 rebounds and 2.7 assists per game and was named to the First Team All-[[West Coast Conference]]. Following the season, Ayayi declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] and forgo his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web |last=Coleman |first=Madeline |title=Gonzaga Star Joel Ayayi Declares for 2021 NBA Draft |url=https://www.si.com/college/2021/04/10/gonzaga-star-joel-ayayi-declares-2021-nba-draft |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=4 June 2021 |date=9 April 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Washington Wizards (2021–2022)=== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Ayayi signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] on 3 August 2021. Under the terms of the deal he was to split time between the Lakers and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[South Bay Lakers]].{{cite web |title=Lakers Sign Joel Ayayi and Austin Reaves to Two-Way Contracts |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-sign-joel-ayayi-austin-reaves-two-way-contracts |website=Los Angeles Lakers |access-date=3 August 2021}} On 15 October, he was waived by Los Angeles{{cite web|title=Lakers Make Training Camp Cuts|date=October 15, 2021|website=NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-make-training-camp-cuts-211015|access-date=October 16, 2021}} and two days later, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web |title=Wizards claim Joel Ayayi |url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-claim-joel-ayayi-101721 |website=NBA.com |access-date=October 17, 2021 |date=October 17, 2021}} Ayayi was then later waived on 8 March 2022.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/players/transactions|title=NBA Transactions|website=nba.com|date=March 8, 2022|access-date=March 8, 2022}} [[File:Joël Ayayi.jpg|thumb|260px|Ayayi with the [[Washington Wizards]] in 2021]] ===Capital City Go-Go (2022)=== On 11 March 2022 Ayayi was reacquired by the [[Capital City Go-Go]].{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League Transactions|date=March 11, 2022|access-date=March 11, 2022}} Ayayi joined the [[Atlanta Hawks]] for the [[2022 NBA Summer League]].{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Hawks 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612737/hawks |access-date=July 5, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} ===Lakeland Magic (2022–2023)=== On 3 November 2022 Ayayi was named to the opening night roster for the [[Osceola Magic|Lakeland Magic]].{{cite web|title=Lakeland Magic Announce 2022-23 Opening Night Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/lakeland-magic-announce-2022-23-opening-night-roster/n-5895510|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=November 3, 2022|access-date=November 3, 2022}} ===Nanterre 92 (2023–2024)=== On 23 July 2023 Ayayi signed with [[Nanterre 92]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].{{cite web|first=Dario|last=Skerletic|title=Nanterre 92 lands Joel Ayayi|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/nanterre-92-lands-joel-ayayi/|website=Sportando.basketball|date=July 23, 2023|access-date=July 24, 2023}} ===JL Bourg (2024–2025)=== On May 31, 2024, he signed with [[JL Bourg]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.jlbourg-basket.com/2024/05/31/joel-ayayi-de-nanterre-a-bourg-en-bresse/|title=Joël Ayayi, une saison à la JL Bourg|last=|first=|date=May 31, 2024|website=jlbourg-basket.com|publisher=|language=fr|access-date=June 2, 2024}} ===Paris Basketball (2025–present)=== On July 3, 2025, he signed with [[Paris Basketball]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].{{Cite tweet |user=ParisBasketball |number=1940759752440795301 |title=Welcome Joel Ayayi}} ==National team career== Ayayi holds [[Multiple citizenship|dual citizenship]] to France and his parents' home country of [[Benin]], but he plays basketball for the French national teams.{{cite web |last1=Meehan |first1=Jim |title=Gonzaga redshirt sophomore Joel Ayayi tries to carve out role among deep roster |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2018/oct/13/gonzaga-redshirt-sophomore-joel-ayayi-tries-to-car/ |website=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |accessdate=23 September 2019 |date=13 October 2018}} At the [[2016 FIBA U16 European Championship]] in [[Radom]], Poland, he averaged 11.3 points and 6.7 rebounds per game for France.{{cite web |last1=Woodburn |first1=Peter |title=Joel Ayayi playing for France in the FIBA U18 European Championships |url=https://www.slipperstillfits.com/2018/7/26/17617134/fiba-u18-european-championships-france-roster-joel-ayayi#comments |publisher=The Slipper Still Fits |accessdate=23 September 2019 |date=26 July 2018}} Ayayi led his team to a bronze medal at the [[2018 FIBA U18 European Championship]] in [[Latvia]]. After averaging 15.7 points per game, he was named to the All-Star Five.{{cite web |title=Ayayi and Petrusev Shine at FIBA U18 European Championship |url=https://gozags.com/news/2018/8/9/mens-basketball-ayayi-and-petrusev-shine-at-fiba-u18-european-championship.aspx |publisher=Gonzaga University Athletics |accessdate=23 September 2019 |date=6 August 2018}} Ayayi helped France win bronze at the [[2019 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup]] in [[Heraklion]], Greece, where he earned All-Star Five honors. He averaged 20.9 points, 5.6 rebounds, and 3.4 assists per game and led all scorers with 33 points in a [[Third place playoff|bronze medal game]] against [[Lithuania men's national under-18 and under-19 basketball team|Lithuania]].{{cite web |title=Gonzaga's Oumar Ballo and Joel Ayayi make All-Star Five at FIBA World Cup |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2019/jul/07/gonzagas-oumar-ballo-and-joel-ayayi-make-all-star-/ |website=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |accessdate=23 September 2019 |date=7 July 2019}} ==Career
